entries.definition: the series of jobs and work experiences in someone’s life
entries.example: She began her career in a small design office.

entries.definition: a person paid to work for an organization
entries.example: Each employee receives a copy of the safety rules.

entries.definition: a person or organization that hires workers
entries.example: My employer offers training during working hours.

entries.definition: a person you work with
entries.example: A colleague helped me understand the new ordering system.

entries.definition: a meeting to assess a person for a job
entries.example: I prepared examples of teamwork before the interview.

entries.definition: knowledge or skill gained by doing something
entries.example: Her experience in customer service helped the team.

entries.definition: learning intended to develop skills for an activity
entries.example: The shop provides training for every new assistant.

entries.definition: a formal agreement with stated responsibilities
entries.example: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.

entries.definition: a regular fixed payment for work
entries.example: The job advertisement lists the monthly salary.

entries.definition: payment for work usually calculated by hours or days
entries.example: The workers discussed a fair hourly wage.

entries.definition: money received from work or other sources
entries.example: The family plans its spending around a regular income.

entries.definition: a plan for how much money can be spent
entries.example: Our budget includes rent, food, transport, and savings.

entries.definition: money spent for a particular need or activity
entries.example: Travel was the largest expense during the project.

entries.definition: money left after the costs of a business are paid
entries.example: The bakery used part of its profit to repair the oven.

entries.definition: the amount by which costs exceed money received
entries.example: The damaged delivery caused a small financial loss.

entries.definition: a person or organization receiving a professional service
entries.example: The designer asked the client to explain her needs.

entries.definition: someone who buys goods or services
entries.example: The customer asked whether the shoes came in another size.

entries.definition: a person responsible for organizing people or work
entries.example: The manager changed the schedule after listening to staff.

entries.definition: the people working for an organization
entries.example: The staff helped move the books before opening time.

entries.definition: a group working together toward a shared aim
entries.example: Our team divided the tasks before starting the repair.

entries.definition: a particular piece of work to be done
entries.example: Checking the addresses is my first task each morning.

entries.definition: a duty to look after something or do something properly
entries.example: Keeping the customer records safe is a shared responsibility.

entries.definition: something you are expected or required to do
entries.example: One duty of the receptionist is welcoming visitors.

entries.definition: a scheduled period of work
entries.example: My evening shift begins after the afternoon team leaves.

entries.definition: a situation that makes something possible
entries.example: The workshop gave me an opportunity to meet local employers.

entries.definition: a move to a more responsible job
entries.example: She received a promotion after leading two successful projects.

entries.definition: to formally ask to be considered for something
entries.example: I plan to apply for the assistant position.

entries.definition: to give someone paid work
entries.example: The company hopes to hire two new technicians.

entries.definition: to receive money in return for work
entries.example: He can earn extra money by repairing bicycles.

entries.definition: to use money to pay for something
entries.example: We should spend less on unnecessary printing.

entries.definition: to have enough money to pay for something
entries.example: Our small office cannot afford a second printer yet.

entries.definition: to receive something with the intention of returning it
entries.example: May I borrow your calculator until lunch?

entries.definition: to give something for someone to return later
entries.example: The library can lend equipment to local study groups.

entries.definition: to have a duty to pay money back
entries.example: I still owe the supplier for last month’s order.

entries.definition: to return money that was borrowed
entries.example: We agreed to repay the loan in small amounts.

entries.definition: a record showing that something has been paid for
entries.example: Keep the receipt if you may need a refund.

entries.definition: a document requesting payment for goods or services
entries.example: The invoice lists the number of repaired computers.

entries.definition: money given to pay what is owed
entries.example: The final payment is due after delivery.

entries.definition: something bought or the act of buying
entries.example: This purchase will help us store the tools safely.

entries.definition: something made or grown to be sold
entries.example: The product label explains how to use the cleaner.

entries.definition: work done to help or supply other people
entries.example: The repair service collects broken equipment on Mondays.

entries.definition: how good or well made something is
entries.example: We check the quality of every repaired bicycle.

entries.definition: the amount or number of something
entries.example: The order form asks for the quantity of each item.

entries.definition: the act of bringing goods to a place
entries.example: The delivery arrived before the shop opened.

entries.definition: an amount available for use
entries.example: The clinic keeps a supply of clean gloves.

entries.definition: how much people want a product or service
entries.example: Demand for warm coats increased when the weather changed.

entries.definition: a written announcement giving information
entries.example: A notice beside the door explains the new opening hours.

entries.definition: to put a new thing in place of an old one
entries.example: We need to replace the damaged cable today.

entries.definition: to make something broken work again
entries.example: The technician will repair the screen this afternoon.

entries.definition: money returned after a purchase is canceled or returned
entries.example: The store offered a refund for the broken lamp.
